author: Cruna
quote:
This is NOT a GTA game.
It's a lie dressed up as GTA.
The whole point of these games were playing them exactly the way you want.
It used to be an escape from reality power fantasy.
It was funny, the writing was amazing, the main characters were always really cool
Now we have incredibly BORING protagonists, braindead writing and dialogues, you can't steal cars or shoot your guns whenever you feel like. 
What happened?
As a game, maybe it's a 4/10 (might climb to a 6 if they fix all the bugs)
As a GTA game, this is a 0/10. This is yet another hijacked title by dumb people who have no clue about the IP. GTA-Veilguard.

author: Cruna
quote:
Survival Horror. Why do we love these games? What are we expecting from a game of this genre when we first hit the play button? To see a freak show with grotesque monsters in a chilly environment? We love this genre, because it's not about the monsters, it's not about the setting really, it's about the player. While our emotions are amplified in a world where we can't predict what's waiting for us behind the corner, we feel more and more alive because we behave here as naturally as we would if we were really there. We would hide, we would listen for noises, we would walk with caution, and try to survive.
This game really brings us what we were hoping for. The beast is as majestic and smart, as I always imagined to be. Alan Dean Foster wrote some very good book adaptations of the movies and even enhanced the world created by Ridley Scott. It was about time, for the gaming industry to approach the concept with some vision.
Level design, atmosphere: captures the soul of the '79 movie without a doubt, also it's a bit familiar to those who played Dead Space (those guys could have made a mean Alien game also...I think). While the game does not innovate in many areas regarding the level design it gets the job done to create the setting for your deadly adventure through the station.
Musical score, art style, every little gizmo, CRT screen,everything shows that the designers were working hard to stay true to the original concept of Alien, the movie where all started.
If you are fan of the Alien series, pick up this game, it's worth it. If you are not, it is still one of the best survival horror games released lately, even if you don't feel that nostalgic scent of the original movie.
There are a few issues we can talk about... Facial animations are pretty stiff and unrealistic, lip sync is mediocre at best in cutscenes and plain bad otherwise. But this visual issues are not a big problem because we are not really here for that. And there is the story... while it's pretty good, I really feel like they should have been bolder when writing it. When someone tries too hard not to break any element that makes the game a true integration in the Alien universe somehow is too cautious when writing a story and any writer would suffer of the lack of freedom in their creativity.
Bottom line is: This is that type of game that will stay in your heart even when you are not playing, and every moment is a thrill when you are. I can only say: Thank you for that crew that finally brought us the Alien in it's true splendor in a game.
